provenance.description: Wilderness or Desert. Dry, rounded hills stretch across the landscape, cut by gullies with little vegetation. Look at this landscape as you picture the wilderness and discuss the word you will use for it.

provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Images · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Sandals. Here is a full view of a person wearing sandals and holding a wooden staff under a shaded shelter. Look down at the feet to see how the sandals are worn.

provenance.title: Sandals
provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Images · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Sandals. Here is a close view of sandals on a person’s feet. Look at the open toes, the straps around the feet and ankles, and the buckle.

provenance.title: Nazareth and Judea
provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Maps · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Nazareth and Judea. Find Nazareth in the region labeled Galilee. Then follow the blue Jordan River toward the Dead Sea, and find Judea and Jerusalem. The black arrows are labeled travels of Jesus. Use these labels to orient yourself to Galilee, Nazareth, and the Jordan River area.

provenance.title: Locations in the Book of Mark
provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Maps · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Locations in the Book of Mark. The large blue area on the left is the Mediterranean Sea. Look inland to the pear-shaped blue lake just above the middle of the map. That is the Sea of Galilee. From its bottom, trace the thin, winding blue line down to the long blue Dead Sea near the bottom of the map. That line is the Jordan River. Blue lines mark rivers; dashed lines mark roads. Around the river are Galilee, Nazareth, Judea, and Jerusalem.

provenance.title: Aerial View of Judea and Jerusalem
provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Maps · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Aerial View of Judea and Jerusalem. This illustrated terrain view shows hills and valleys around Judea and Jerusalem, with the Jordan River and the Dead Sea. Find Jerusalem and notice the raised land and the lower river valley as you picture the setting.

provenance.title: Important Locations in Jerusalem
provenance.source: Familiarization, Internalization, Articulation (FIA) Maps · CC BY-SA 4.0
provenance.description: Important Locations in Jerusalem. This map outlines Jerusalem and labels the Temple, the Mount of Olives, and nearby places. Find Jerusalem inside the heavy black outline, then look across the blue river line toward the Mount of Olives.

provenance.expectedSpokenText: Stop here and look at a picture and map of the Jordan River as a group. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and show the translation team a photo of sandals. I will pause the audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of ceremonies or rituals does your culture have to show that someone is starting a new way of life or an important work? How are these ceremonies the same or different than baptism?

I will pause the audio here so you can discuss these questions as a group.
provenance.transition: I will pause the audio here so you can discuss these questions as a group.

provenance.expectedSpokenText: I will pause the audio here while you show your group a map that shows the region of Galilee that includes Nazareth and the Jordan River area.
I will pause the audio here while you show your group a picture of the Jordan river and a picture of the wilderness.
I will pause the audio here while you show your group a map of Judea and Jerusalem.
I will pause the audio here while you act out the passage.
I will pause the audio here while you act out the passage a second time.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for gospel. Look up gospel in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for Messiah, or Christ. Look up Messiah or Christ in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what phrase you will use for Son of God. For more information about Son of God, refer to the Master Glossary. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word you will use for prophet. For more information about prophet, refer to the Master Glossary. I will pause the audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of a desert/ wilderness as a group. Discuss what word you will use for wilderness. For more information about wilderness, refer to the Master Glossary. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word you will use for Lord. For more information about Lord, refer to the Master Glossary. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for baptism and repentance. Look up baptism and repentance in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for sin. Look up sin in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for Holy Spirit. Look up Holy Spirit in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for heaven. Look up heaven in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for Satan. Look up Satan in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.
Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for angels. Look up angels in the Master Glossary for more information. I will pause the audio here.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

I will pause the audio here so your group can retell the passage together.
provenance.transition: I will pause the audio here so your group can retell the passage together.

provenance.expectedSpokenText:
Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

I will pause the audio here so each group member can retell the whole passage.
provenance.transition: I will pause the audio here so each group member can retell the whole passage.

provenance.expectedSpokenText:
Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

I will pause the audio here so your group can decide which retelling, or parts of different retellings, you prefer.
provenance.transition: I will pause the audio here so your group can decide which retelling, or parts of different retellings, you prefer.
